item: Repair record degrades per run; a repaired row exports as inherited (diagnostics rank 14, follow-up to #1281 and #1285)
status: SHIPPED (field effect appears at each instance's next boot)
summary: One unreadable repair-run record no longer stops the boot repair or the report: the run is kept byte for byte, never replaced or confirmed, left out of the counts and named (repair_runs_unreadable) while the readable runs carry on; --revert-repairs stays fail closed and names the run. A failed run is marked superseded only when none of its left-out sources reads the state that run would have written; unconfirmed repairs are counted per domain from the newest record; a repaired row exports as inherited (basis.repaired_exported_as_inherited); a second revert marks records a failed marking write left unmarked; Row A and the manual say how to read laundered_total after an import. Also from the Opus review of #1285: the forced re-check count restarts when a newer attempt disagrees, and two pins (the spare-slot path, the contested-slot turn across passes).
